\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{परिवर्तयति} (parivartayati)}{परिवर्तयति (parivartayati)}]{\sk{परिवर्तयति} (parivartayati) — changes}

\label{lesson:SA-C176-parivartayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for endures, then the Sanskrit for tries.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{परिवर्तयति}}
\textbf{\sk{परिवर्तयति}} — \emph{parivartayati} — \textquotedblleft{}changes\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{parivartayati} is built on \emph{pari} \textquotedblleft{}around\textquotedblright{} and the root √vṛt, \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{} (MW), with the causative ending \emph{-aya-}: it means \textquotedblleft{}makes something turn round\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}changes\textquotedblright{}. MW compares √vṛt with Latin \emph{vertere}, \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parivartayati}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parivartayati}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{parivartayati}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for endures, then the Sanskrit for tries, then say \emph{parivartayati} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{निवेदयति} (nivedayati)}{निवेदयति (nivedayati)}]{\sk{निवेदयति} (nivedayati) — reports, submits}

\label{lesson:SA-C176-nivedayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for tries, then the Sanskrit for changes.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{निवेदयति}}
\textbf{\sk{निवेदयति}} — \emph{nivedayati} — \textquotedblleft{}reports, submits\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nivedayati} is the causative of \emph{ni-} with the root √vid, \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{} (MW): it means \textquotedblleft{}makes known\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}reports, presents\textquotedblright{}. The root is inherited from Indo-European; MW compares Latin \emph{vidēre}, \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{आमन्त्रयति} (āmantrayati)}{आमन्त्रयति (āmantrayati)}]{\sk{आमन्त्रयति} (āmantrayati) — invites}

\label{lesson:SA-C176-amantrayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for changes, then the Sanskrit for reports.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{आमन्त्रयति}}
\textbf{\sk{आमन्त्रयति}} — \emph{āmantrayati} — \textquotedblleft{}invites\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{āmantrayati} is \emph{ā-} \textquotedblleft{}towards\textquotedblright{} with \emph{mantrayate}, \textquotedblleft{}speaks, takes counsel\textquotedblright{}, which MW calls a verb made from the noun \emph{mantra}, built on the root √man \textquotedblleft{}to think\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL 1242 records \textquotedblleft{}summons\textquotedblright{} for it in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa and \textquotedblleft{}invites\textquotedblright{} in the Mahābhārata; it lives on as Gujarati \emph{āmãtravũ}, \textquotedblleft{}invites\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{शोधयति} (śodhayati)}{शोधयति (śodhayati)}]{\sk{शोधयति} (śodhayati) — cleans, corrects}

\label{lesson:SA-C176-sodhayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for reports, then the Sanskrit for invites.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{शोधयति}}
\textbf{\sk{शोधयति}} — \emph{śodhayati} — \textquotedblleft{}cleans, corrects\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{śodhayati} is the causative of the root √śudh, \textquotedblleft{}to be purified, become pure\textquotedblright{} (MW). So it comes from \textquotedblleft{}makes pure\textquotedblright{}, which covers both cleaning a thing and correcting a text.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{पूरयति} (pūrayati)}{पूरयति (pūrayati)}]{\sk{पूरयति} (pūrayati) — fills}

\label{lesson:SA-C176-purayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for invites, then the Sanskrit for cleans.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{पूरयति}}
\textbf{\sk{पूरयति}} — \emph{pūrayati} — \textquotedblleft{}fills\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pūrayati} is built on the root √pṝ, \textquotedblleft{}to fill\textquotedblright{} (MW), and is listed in CDIAL 8335. The root is inherited from Indo-European: MW compares Latin \emph{plēnus} and English \emph{full}. CDIAL gives Punjabi \emph{pūrnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to fill\textquotedblright{}, as one of its descendants.
\end{cousinweb}
